confidence.rationale: The doctrine is now explicit and contract-tested as a strategic reservation; future product work must independently validate the architecture.

decision_rules: Keep one canonical intelligence and control core for the four product surfaces.
Allow environment-specific UI, adapters, drivers, packaging, runtime, and capabilities only without forking central truth.
Require a separate approved scope, contract, permission, isolation, recovery, and human review before any future surface becomes operational.

evidence_refs.claim: One canonical core and four named product surfaces are defined without implementation claims.
The doctrine, non-capability boundary, and canonical index link are contract-tested.

failure_modes: Treat four surfaces as independent products and fork identity, knowledge, permissions, evidence, or lifecycle.
Treat a strategic surface name as proof of a current OS, mobile, runtime, or integration capability.
Use lock-in or data seizure as a substitute for earned utility and trust.

notes: A surface cannot infer authority, permission, or capability from presentation alone.
A canonical core gives future surfaces a shared continuity and provenance boundary.

preconditions: The shared core and each surface are named as architectural responsibilities, not assumed implementations.
Current contracts remain the authority for present capabilities.
procedure: Record the canonical core responsibilities once.
Name each surface and its environment-specific concerns without duplicating the core doctrine.
Mark future-only capabilities and define the maturity order before implementation planning.
Link future documents to the single doctrine and require independent contracts for activation.
recovery: If a future document duplicates or contradicts the doctrine, preserve the canonical document and reconcile the reference.
If a surface proposal expands product authority, pause it at a new contract frontier.
Do not delete historical strategic documents to make the current doctrine appear older.
stop_conditions: Stop if documentation is used to claim a current OS, mobile app, runtime, execution, endpoint, or integration.
Stop if a surface requires independent authority or a fork of canonical knowledge and contracts.
Stop for unresolved ownership, security, privacy, or human-authority decisions.
summary: A single canonical core preserves shared authority and continuity while four future surfaces adapt execution to different environments.
title: One core, four surfaces preserve canonical authority
validation: The canonical doctrine names all four surfaces, shared core responsibilities, principles, and non-capability boundary.
The index links one doctrine and does not create a parallel future-surface definition.
